review_target.head: working tree (uncommitted RND-321 implementation plus QA artifacts)
review_target.diff_scope: RND-321 implementation changes span identity/access-request models, auth and user routes, admin UI/i18n, migration 0034, and focused tests. This verdict/report pair is an explicitly authorized QA artifact. No production deployment, CI/CD, or source-code remediation was performed by QA.

evidence: Fresh disposable PostgreSQL database wecom_archive_rnd321_ac8_c8aa017e3ca9_test: direct SELECT current_database() and the Alembic engine connection both returned exactly that database name before any migration or seed write.

Alembic migrated the isolated database to 0033; QA seeded one legacy admin_users row with invite_status=access_requested; then ran 0034 -> 0033. Revisions observed: 0033 before seed, 0034 after upgrade, 0033 after downgrade.

SELECT * snapshot of the seeded admin_users row was exactly equal both immediately after 0034 and after downgrade to 0033; admin_login_identities count for that legacy row was 0 after upgrade. The QA-created database was deleted after the assertions passed.

commands.command: env -u DATABASE_URL ./.venv/bin/python -m pytest backend/tests/test_rnd286_user_admin.py backend/tests/test_users_page.py backend/tests/test_rnd321_qr_login.py -q
isolated PostgreSQL AC-8 harness with DATABASE_URL set for the Alembic process
commands.result: EXIT=0 (direct and Alembic current_database() matched the unique disposable DB; 0033 -> seed -> 0034 -> 0033; legacy identity count=0; full admin_users row equal after upgrade and downgrade; QA DB deleted)

notes: This is the fourth human-requested QA execution; qa_attempt remains 3 because the repository schema caps it at 3. `no_commit_or_push` is false only because origin/main..HEAD already contains d90801c; QA created no commit and performed no push. The earlier QA execution incident is recorded in tasks/RND-321-qa-report.md. Haisu directed that local wecom_archive remain at 0034 and receive no further QA writes or migrations; this AC-8 run complied by using and deleting a newly created disposable database. Human WeCom QR E2E remains a post-deployment touchpoint and is not part of the completed local migration gate.
